title: Phone desk stop: the desk is hidden behind the card
evidence: review/runs/2026-10-17-g2/desk-pixel7.png: the card covers the bottom 59% of the frame and the desk with its postcard, envelope, catalogue and ledger is not visible at all; only the beam and the end-wall line show. The committed CI baseline tests/e2e/__screenshots__/visual.spec.ts/stop-desk-pixel7.png shows the same. Stats: the desk camera is identical on both viewports (position [0, 1.6, -64], target [0, 1.1, -67.5]), so the 36% portrait framing point holds the look-at at 1.1 m, above the desk top, and the desk projects below the card's top edge. D2 anchor 1 (covered by the card).
expected: On portrait phones the desk top and its four objects sit above the card, near the 36% framing point, like the exhibit cases (EXPERIENCE section 8 gift shop, ART_DIRECTION D2). Options for R4 and R6: a lower look-at for the desk stop on portrait, a desk-specific portrait framing point, or a shorter phone desk card (links in a row, closing line hidden).
check: Capture desk on pixel7 (CAPTURE_STOPS=desk ... --project=pixel7): every desk object is visible above the card; window.__MUSEUM__.screenPos('desk') y is above the card's getBoundingClientRect().top; rebaseline stop-desk-pixel7.

title: Desktop story dialog: HUD, rail and wing controls show through the panel
evidence: review/runs/2026-10-17-g2/safe-sip-dialog-desktop.png: 'VOLUNTEER & LEADERSHIP WING, 1 OF 2', 'Return to the aisle Esc' and 'No. V1, Tamper Evident' are drawn crisp through the panel on top of the dek and the role block; the rail line and dots run through the bullets. verafin-dialog-desktop.png: the rail tooltip sits beside the role line, rail year labels cross the bullets, and the Classic view button shows under Close. The panel is --panel (86% alpha) with a 14 px backdrop blur, but the HUD behind it is not blurred. A probe page in the same Chromium (fixed text under a showModal dialog with the same background and blur) does blur, so this is not a headless limitation. The CI dialog baselines do not catch it (the canvas is masked and the HUD is not in them).
expected: Dialog text sits on a calm panel: nothing behind it reads as text (D3 anchor 5). Either hide the HUD, rail and wing controls while a story is open on desktop (html[data-sheet='open'] or the store's openId), or find why the backdrop blur skips them and fall back to --panel-solid.
check: Open verafin and safe-sip stories at 1440x900 (CAPTURE_DIALOGS=1): no HUD, rail or wing text is visible inside the panel; an e2e assertion that the rail and wing chip are hidden or visually covered while the dialog is open.

title: 3D wall and door titles clipped by the viewport and covered by HUD buttons
evidence: pixel7: projects-door-pixel7.png PDF button covers the middle of PROJECTS (reads PROJ...CTS); volunteer-door-pixel7.png the wing title runs under and through the PDF and Classic buttons (DERSP inside the Classic outline); verafin-pixel7.png 01 under the Classic button and NASDAQ VERA cut by the right edge; mysa-pixel7.png 02 under the year chip; safe-sip-pixel7.png V1 under Return to the aisle. desktop: verafin-desktop.png 01 clipped by the viewport top and under the Resume button; projects-door-desktop.png PROJECTS cut at the top edge; volunteer-door-desktop.png title runs off the top right under the Resume button; mysa-desktop.png 02 clipped at the top.
expected: Each wall or door title sits fully inside the frame, below the HUD controls (clear of their bounding boxes), above or beside its case (D2 anchor 5: 'the wall title reads above it'). Likely a lower title height or a smaller size on portrait, or a camera tilt, for R3 with R4.
check: Captures of the seven slice stops on both viewports: every 3D title is complete and none intersects a HUD control's bounding box (compare the label's projected bounds with the HUD rects in an e2e check, or by eye on the capture).

title: Tier medium floor washes out to a flat bright plane in the wings
evidence: projects-door-pixel7.png and volunteer-door-pixel7.png: the wing floor is a uniform warm grey (about #5a5048) over 35 to 40% of the frame; safe-sip-pixel7.png: the same flat planes on both sides of the plinth; verafin-pixel7.png and the CI baseline stop-verafin-desktop.png (tier medium) show a smaller wedge at lower right. At tier high (reflector floor) the same rooms stay dark (projects-door-desktop.png). Phones get tier medium, so this is what most mobile visitors see. D1 anchor 1 to 3 (washed, evenly lit).
expected: The medium floor reads as dark polished floor with warm pools only where the baked lightmap puts them, close in value to the high tier. Likely the env reflection at grazing angles (roughness 0.22, envMapIntensity 0.6, the ceiling strip Lightformer); R3 with R2 for any material token change.
check: Capture projects-door, volunteer-door and safe-sip on pixel7: mean luminance of the floor region within about 15% of the desktop high capture; no flat area brighter than the light pool peak.

title: Plinths render as pure black voids
evidence: verafin-desktop.png, safe-sip-desktop.png, safe-sip-pixel7.png: the plinth front is close to #000 with no value step from the dark floor, so the case looks pasted onto a black hole; on pixel7 it is a black rectangle 400 px tall between case and card.
expected: The plinth (#1F1F24) reads as a solid object one step above the floor: a faint top-edge highlight or the wall wash catching its front, so the case is grounded (D1 anchor 5).
check: Capture verafin desktop: plinth front mean value visibly above the floor beside it; the plinth edge is visible in the 320 px thumbnail.

title: Beam cones read as opaque grey shafts
evidence: desk-desktop.png: the beam is a near-opaque grey column, the strongest shape in the frame, washing the end-wall line; lobby-desktop.png: a bright wedge top right behind the HUD buttons and portrait; verafin-desktop.png: the right wall is washed grey by the cone. The beam material is additive at opacity 0.035, so either cones overlap or the brightness comes from the wall wash under them.
expected: Beams are a faint suggestion of light in the air (ART_DIRECTION lighting recipe), never brighter than the pool they feed.
check: Capture desk and lobby desktop: the beam region is darker than the end-wall label and the floor pool; the portrait and HUD corner are no longer washed.

title: Vertical streak noise on the aisle walls at grazing angles
evidence: projects-door-desktop.png (x 0 to 560, y 0 to 500) and mysa-desktop.png (x 0 to 430): fine vertical streaks on the far wall, clear when brightened (out/wp19/streak.png, scratch). Looks like minification aliasing of the wall wash or seam texture without mipmaps or anisotropy (a hypothesis, not confirmed in code).
expected: Walls at grazing angles read as smooth dark panels with seams every 2 m (D1 anchor 1 lists noise).
check: Capture projects-door desktop at tier high: no high-frequency vertical pattern on the left wall when the region is brightened 3x.

title: Wing wall titles collide with the beam and the case
evidence: projects-door-desktop.png: the beam cone cuts the I of FINANCE and the case covers TRACKER; volunteer-door-desktop.png: the beam splits SOFTWARE and the case covers ST.; safe-sip-desktop.png: the beam crosses ENACTUS MEMORIAL. The wash arch behind each title is offset from the text and narrower than it.
expected: Each wing title reads whole above its case, centered on its wash, with the beam passing in front of the wall below the text.
check: Capture the two door stops and safe-sip: every wing title is unbroken and centered on its wash.

evidence: safe-sip-desktop.png and safe-sip-thumb.png: the frostedGlass cup reads as an opaque near-white cylinder, the brightest thing in the case; the stepped lid, the Pico W board and the tamper ring are not legible at stop distance; the edge-on yaw arc reads as a stray horizontal wire beside the cup. R2's WP-13 verdict notes flagged the same for G2.

title: Gallery pages do not declare color-scheme: dark
evidence: Every desktop capture has a 15 px band at the right edge (x 1425 to 1440): the reserved stable scrollbar gutter (src/overlay/ScrollTrack.module.css). Only [data-page='classic'] sets color-scheme, so on Windows and Linux with classic scrollbars a light system scrollbar will sit beside the dark gallery. Headless Chromium hides scrollbars, so the captures show only the gutter.
expected: The always-dark gallery (EXPERIENCE section 7.10) declares color-scheme: dark on its pages (or a scrollbar-color in tokens), so native scrollbars and form controls render dark.
check: grep -n 'color-scheme: dark' src/app/global.css; on Chromium with --hide-scrollbars off, the scrollbar at 1440x900 is dark.
